title: Pseudogap formation in the moderate correlated layered attractive Hubbard model
authors: A. V. Belov, A. N. Rubtsov, B. Krippa
abstract: We consider the layered attractive Hubbard model with a moderate interaction strength at quarter filling. The Green's function, self-energy, and density of states are calculated for relatively large clusters using the fluctuating local field method within the approximation of vanishing effective interaction. The emergence of a pseudogap is demonstrated for the cluster system, and it is shown that integration over the fluctuating field is equivalent to the summation of zero-mode ladder diagrams above critical temperature. For the large layered system, a pseudogap in the density of states is obtained within a cluster scheme that treats the coupling between layers as a static $U(1)$ symmetry-breaking field.
summary: This paper theoretically investigates pseudogap formation in a layered attractive Hubbard model using the Fluctuating Local Field (FLF) method. The authors demonstrate that this non-perturbative approach captures a persistent pseudogap structure in the density of states, which remains visible even when mean-field theory predicts the superconducting gap has closed due to thermal fluctuations.
main_problem: The study investigates the formation of a pseudogap phase in a layered attractive Hubbard model, aiming to understand its origin relative to superconducting fluctuations.
main_result: The Fluctuating Local Field (FLF) method successfully demonstrates the emergence of a persistent pseudogap structure in the density of states, which persists even when mean-field theory predicts the gap should close above $T_c$.
method: The primary theoretical tool is the Fluctuating Local Field (FLF) method, applied within a cluster scheme to calculate Green's functions and self-energies non-perturbatively.
model_or_system: The system modeled is the layered attractive Hubbard model at quarter filling. The Hamiltonian includes hopping terms ($t$ intralayer, $t_2$ interlayer) and an interaction term, analyzed using a cluster approach extended to the infinite lattice via a static symmetry-breaking field $\Delta$.
key_observables: Green's function (GF), self-energy ($\Sigma$), Density of States (DOS), and the superconducting gap structure.
important_parameters: Moderate correlation strength ($|U|/t \approx 1$ to $2$) and weak interlayer coupling ($t_2$).
main_assumptions: The analysis relies on the FLF method, which uses a static approximation for the fluctuating field ($\Delta$), and in some contexts, assumes $\Sigma' \approx 0$ when treating zero modes.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the layered hopping structure; DOS plots compare mean-field vs. FLF results showing pseudogap persistence above $T_c$; Self-energy plots show agreement below $T_c$.
paper_structure: The paper progresses by defining the model and applying the FLF method to finite clusters, then extrapolating these results using a static $\Delta$ approximation to describe the infinite layered system, culminating in comparisons of DOS and self-energies across different temperature regimes.
why_interesting: The non-perturbative treatment of superconducting fluctuations via the FLF method provides advanced theoretical insight into spectral weight renormalization and gap physics, which is highly relevant for understanding strongly correlated materials like cuprates.

figures.caption: FIG. 1: Schematic illustration of the layered system. Black solid lines denote intralayer hopping, while grey dotted lines denote interlayer hopping.

FIG. 2: Density of states (DOS) for temperatures below, near and above mean-field transition for 8 × 8 (first row) with Tc ≈0.14 and 16 × 16 (second row) with Tc ≈0.1. Red lines is mean-field DOS, blue - FLF-0 DOS, green - FLF-1 DOS, black slashed line is Fermi level. At this line, formation of a gap and a pseudogap is clearly seen. DOS from FLF-1 with Fock correction is nearly the same as DOS in FLF-0

FIG. 3: Self-energy in FLF method for tempetoratures below, near and above mean-field transition for 16 × 16 cluster with Tc ≈0.1. In (a) FLF self-energy is compared with mean-field - red color, in (c) - is compared with zero-mode ladder approximation - also red color. Square markers denote imaginary part of self-energy, cross markers - real part

FIG. 4: Dependence of order parameter on temperature with different exchange couplings for 16 × 16 cluster. Pink circles - 0.1, violet triangles - 0.2, green squares - 0.3 and green crosses - 0.3 for 8 × 8 cluster

FIG. 5: Density of states for large lattice near quarter-filling from discussed cluster scheme. Transition temperature from mean-field Tc ≈0.113. Violet lines are DOS on base of the cluster with sizes 8 × 8, green lines - cluster with sizes 16 × 16, pink lines - mean-field result, black dashed line - Fermi-level
